slides.label: 01 / SRE Lens
slides.title: SRE Lens asks the right specialists.
slides.intro: One request goes to Lens. It asks only the permitted specialists needed for the question.
slides.takeaway: Delegate by the question and permission. Return one answer with its sources.

scenarios.label: Cross-system

slides.notes: Start with Workload incident. Follow the single question into Lens, then the two selected delegations and their return findings. Select Data question and both directions switch to Data only. Cross-system selects all three. The unselected routes fade; the cards remain visible as available inventory, never completed work. The combined answer is returned to the original caller. This is an offline explanation, not a routing decision or execution receipt. The GitLab/Kubernetes/Data topology is the user-described illustration in showcase.html#lens. The inspected native A2A YAML instead names Grafana, data-compliance and Kubernetes specialists. Open the Lens source to inspect that exact illustrative YAML. It does not install this full topology. No component is identified as Node.js because that name remains unconfirmed.

slides.label: 02 / Scoped evidence
slides.title: An Agent reasons. Its MCP reads.
slides.intro: Each specialist uses its own scoped tool adapter. Backend access belongs to a separate identity and grant.
slides.takeaway: Agent delegation, MCP tool permission and backend read access are separate checks.
slides.notes: These are three illustrative read lanes. The Agent is the specialist that plans and interprets. MCP is its tool interface, not another reasoning agent. Tool names and availability must come from the receiving server discovery response. The source popups list operations by intent rather than inventing deployed tool names. Kubernetes reads remain inside allowed namespaces and RBAC. GitLab reads remain inside approved projects. Data reads use an approved adapter and backend grants. Existing catalog material names Denodo; the PostgreSQL typed adapter is a separate option with explicit limits. Do not treat the two as one installation. The user-described Data specialist does not confirm a Node.js server or a specific backend. No apply, delete, arbitrary SQL, write or remediation action runs here. Return arrows depict bounded source results, not observed live responses.

slides.label: 03 / One evidence-backed answer
slides.title: Combine evidence. Keep the gaps visible.
slides.intro: Each claim keeps its source. Missing or denied evidence stays visible.
slides.takeaway: Unavailable and denied evidence stays unknown. A human chooses the next action.

slides.notes: The scenario status below the diagram explicitly names each source outcome. Source receipt cards are neutral because the existing renderer changes paths and scenario text, not node content. Every source-status path remains active in every scenario. An unavailable or denied receipt still needs to reach Lens as an explicit status. An inactive line cannot stand in for a failure result. Complete means all three illustrative required sources returned, not that the diagnosis is correct or a cause is proven. Partial keeps Kubernetes and Data observations while GitLab-related change information remains unknown. Denied keeps Kubernetes and GitLab observations while Data evidence remains unknown. Each receipt popup includes every scenario with synthetic IDs and provenance. The answer popup shows the different claims and next reads. Never infer an automatic fix, retry, alternate credential or provider switch. Any change belongs to a separate reviewed, human-approved workflow.

slides.notes: DICE can be consumed by an SRE interface or another application/workflow. Input may originate as text or a bounded application payload, but the currently documented runtime example serializes the request in an A2A message part with kind=text. The source popup shows that envelope. This does not claim an implemented typed-payload API or new SDK. API invocation is separate from permission to use a specialist, call an MCP tool or read the backend resource. The reference YAML demonstrates Agent-type delegation and allowedNamespaces namespace opt-in. Namespace selection is not Entra user authorization. Tokens must have the correct audience at each boundary; there is no pass-through JWT assumption. Native delegation alone does not establish that every hop traverses agentgateway. For a real demonstration collect actual invocation, delegation, tool and backend results and correlate observed trace spans. Use actual usage telemetry where present; absent usage, spans or provider receipts remain unknown. All IDs and outputs here are synthetic, with no live counters, latency or cost claims.

question.title: Example questions and specialist selection

routing.title: Lens routing and exact native A2A reference
routing.type: Inspected local illustrative YAML and explicit topology difference
routing.text:
ILLUSTRATIVE TOPOLOGY
The deck follows showcase.html#lens and the user-described GitLab, Kubernetes and Data inventory. Those integrations are not claimed as installed or current.

INSPECTED SOURCE
docs/demos/microsoft-2026-10-15/yaml-walkthrough/04-a2a-orchestrator.yaml names Grafana, data-compliance and Kubernetes specialists, not the complete GitLab/Lens illustration. Agent-type tools demonstrate native delegation. Destination allowedNamespaces is namespace opt-in, separate from caller authentication and backend tool grants. The YAML does not install every tool integration. No live model-backed result is proven by this example.

EXACT REFERENCE YAML
# STEP 04 - Attach specialist agents with A2A

apiVersion: kagent.dev/v1alpha2
kind: Agent  # This is a separate orchestration Agent for the SRE conversation.
metadata:
  name: sre-chat  # SRE talks to this single chatbot rather than opening every specialist separately.
  namespace: team-sre
spec:
  type: Declarative
  description: SRE chatbot delegates investigations to permitted specialists.
  declarative:
    modelConfig: model-garden  # The chatbot uses the same model-garden connection pattern as the triage agent.
    # We instruct it to delegate investigations and combine the cited findings.
    systemMessage: Delegate questions to the relevant permitted specialist. Return one
      cited answer.
    tools:  # These tools are named specialist agents; their own tool permissions remain separate.
    - type: Agent  # An Agent-type tool lets the chatbot delegate a task over A2A.
      agent:
        apiGroup: kagent.dev
        kind: Agent
        name: grafana-evidence  # This specialist supplies Grafana metrics and application telemetry when configured.
        namespace: specialists  # The destination lives in the specialist namespace and must allow the caller.
    - type: Agent
      agent:
        apiGroup: kagent.dev
        kind: Agent
        name: data-compliance  # This specialist supplies approved data, incident or compliance context.
        namespace: specialists
    - type: Agent
      agent:
        apiGroup: kagent.dev
        kind: Agent
        name: kubernetes-triage  # This specialist supplies Kubernetes runtime evidence for the same investigation.
        namespace: specialists
---
# Minimal destination Agent: illustrates namespace opt-in.
# ModelConfig/model-garden in specialists and approved Grafana tools are separate
# prerequisites; this object does not pretend to install that tool integration.
apiVersion: kagent.dev/v1alpha2
kind: Agent  # The second document defines a minimal destination agent, not another chatbot.
metadata:
  name: grafana-evidence  # This name matches the Grafana specialist reference in the first document.
  namespace: specialists
spec:
  type: Declarative
  description: Grafana evidence specialist with explicit caller namespace opt-in.
  allowedNamespaces:  # The destination opts in to permitted cross-namespace Agent references.
    from: Selector  # We choose caller namespaces by a platform-controlled label.
    selector:
      matchLabels:
        team: sre  # The SRE namespace must carry this label; this is separate from Entra authorization.
  declarative:
    modelConfig: model-garden  # This ModelConfig must also exist in the specialists namespace.
    systemMessage: |  # Actual Grafana tools are a prerequisite; this example must report missing evidence honestly.
      Return cited observations from approved evidence.
      Report missing access instead of inventing metrics.

backend-auth.title: Tool access and backend resource authorization
backend-auth.text:
Each lane has two distinct permission checks after Agent delegation.

1. Specialist -> MCP. Permit only the named tools for that specialist and intended scope.
2. MCP -> backend. Use the backend identity and least-privilege resource grants for that operation.

Kubernetes requires the correct service-account/RBAC and namespace/workload restrictions. GitLab requires an approved project read identity. Data requires the configured data principal, views and grants.

For the separate PostgreSQL UAMI option, the reference chain is AKS Workload Identity -> UAMI -> Entra token -> azure-postgresql-auth/psycopg3 -> TLS PostgreSQL. The matching PostgreSQL Entra principal and read grants are required. This is a reference option, not a claim that this deck installs it.

Caller-to-Lens, Lens-to-specialist, specialist-to-MCP and backend resource rights remain distinct. A successful API call does not prove backend authorization. Never assume the same JWT is passed between audiences.

No authorization check runs from this HTML.

permissions.title: Caller and specialist permissions stay separate
permissions.text:
Caller -> Lens
Authenticate the caller and authorize invocation of the intended Lens Agent.

Lens -> specialist
Allow only intended Agent references. The inspected YAML demonstrates Agent-type tools and destination allowedNamespaces namespace-label opt-in. This is not end-user Entra authorization or a blanket tool grant.

Specialist -> MCP -> backend
Require separate permitted operations and backend grants. Inspect the backend authorization source for each lane.

Routing boundary
Native A2A delegation alone does not prove that every hop passes through agentgateway. Verify the installed routing and observed spans before making that claim.

Change boundary
Diagnosis returns observations and a proposed next read. A separate reviewed, human-approved workflow owns any resource-changing action.
